# TxVerify Core

This document describes the TxVerify model of PTX execution (`Core/`) for a reader. It has two kinds of entries. A concept is a Lean definition that the rules are stated over, shown with its doc comment. A rule is a contract block of the model: its statement says in plain words what it requires of programs or executions, its source cites the PTX ISA 9.5 text it rests on, and its direction says how it relates to that text. Interpretations, marked EXT, are readings of the PTX text that the model adopts beyond what the text states. Every entry is generated from the comments of the Lean source by `Tools/coredoc.py` and links to the lines it was generated from. The review guide and the index of all contract blocks are in [Core/README.md](../../Core/README.md).

## Chapters

In reading order:

1. [The program, its values and the launch](program.md): How the model represents a kernel before it runs: the parsed PTX source, its decoding into typed instructions, the values and bytes that registers and memory hold, and the launch that fixes the grid. (33 concepts, 16 rules, 4 EXT notes)
2. [Instructions: families, rules and tables](instructions.md): How a decoded instruction gets its meaning. (13 concepts, 16 rules, 0 EXT notes)
3. [Threads: state, local steps and events](threads.md): How one thread runs: its local state, the registers and local instructions, the events it emits for every other instruction, and the events and executions that collect them. (48 concepts, 38 rules, 11 EXT notes)
4. [Memory model](memory.md): How the model orders memory accesses and decides which values a read may return: byte locations and footprints, scopes, program order, base causality order, the byte-specific model causality order that also covers asynchronous accesses, the reads-from and coherence axioms, and the memory errors (data races, including the exemption for writes of identical values, mixed-size conflicts, unallocated bytes and the shared-memory lifetime). (35 concepts, 14 rules, 4 EXT notes)
5. [Barriers and warp collectives](barriers.md): How the model treats CTA barriers (`bar`, `barrier`), cluster barriers (`barrier.cluster`), cluster membership, and the warp collectives `bar.warp.sync`, `elect.sync`, `shfl.sync`, `vote.sync`, `redux.sync`, `match.sync` and `activemask`, together with the rule that threads of a warp agree on the guard of a uniform instruction. (48 concepts, 34 rules, 11 EXT notes)
6. [mbarrier](mbarrier.md): How the model treats `mbarrier` objects: what each instruction does to an object, which executions are allowed, and what counts as an error. (30 concepts, 14 rules, 4 EXT notes)
7. [Asynchronous copies and tensor maps](async.md): How the model treats the asynchronous engine: bulk copies and tensor copies (TMA), tensor maps and their geometry, multicast, bulk groups and their waits, tensor stores and reductions, and the safety checks that apply to them. (46 concepts, 33 rules, 10 EXT notes)
8. [tcgen05](tcgen05.md): How the model treats the `tcgen05` instructions other than Tensor Memory allocation: the MMA kinds and descriptors, where operands and results lie in shared and Tensor Memory, the cells that loads, stores and copies access, `tcgen05.commit`, the tcgen05 fences, the order in which the Tensor Core performs its accesses and the values it produces. (55 concepts, 33 rules, 8 EXT notes)
9. [Tensor Memory](tmem.md): How the model treats Tensor Memory: how each CTA's allocator allocates and deallocates columns, how relinquishing the permit and cta_group::2 pairs of CTAs work, when an access is covered by an allocation, and what counts as an error. (43 concepts, 17 rules, 4 EXT notes)
10. [Cluster launch control](clc.md): How the model treats `clusterlaunchcontrol`: the arbitration that launches or cancels clusters, the responses to cancellation requests, and their delivery to the CTAs of a cluster. (12 concepts, 6 rules, 0 EXT notes)
11. [Assumptions a kernel may declare](assumptions.md): What a kernel may assume beyond the core rules, and what each kind of assumption makes the model trust. (14 concepts, 11 rules, 1 EXT notes)
12. [Correctness](correctness.md): What it means for a kernel to be correct, how the other chapters fit into that definition, and how far the conclusion carries to real hardware. (22 concepts, 14 rules, 6 EXT notes)
